## Summary

The May 11 and November 7, 2026 wallet guides describe routing Apple Pay and Google Pay with Stripe Orchestration. The separately captured May Orchestration overview already identifies the product as private preview. The November wallet guide adds an email request and a registration example for `orchestration_preview`. This requests access. Approval, processor and wallet setup, and rule activation are separate.

## Wallet and processor compatibility

The November feature-support matrix lists general Apple Pay and Google Pay support for Adyen, Braintree and Worldpay WPG. Its wallet footnote specifies that 3DS is unsupported with Apple Pay or Google Pay DPANs, and Google Pay FPAN is unsupported on Adyen. The wallet guide describes the general routing capability. Consult the matrix for the processor and token combination. [[source-stripe-orchestration-feature-support]]

## Set up and test routing

1. Enable the applicable wallet on the third-party processor according to that processor’s requirements.
2. Configure Stripe through its Apple Pay or Google Pay integration.
3. Configure test routing under **Payments → Orchestration → Rules** in the Dashboard.
4. Test wallet routing. Both captures suggest Payment Links as an optional way to test Apple Pay or Google Pay quickly.

The separate Rules guide scopes activated test rules to their sandbox. Live rules require their own activation. A test configuration supplies no evidence of authorization, capture or settlement. [[source-stripe-orchestration-rules]]

## Saved and customer-present wallet payments

- **Saved mobile-wallet payment method:** Pass `off_session=true` during PaymentIntent confirmation when attempting a charge.
- **Customer present at checkout:** Re-prompt for payment method presentment through the applicable Apple Pay or Google Pay integration. The guide excludes reuse of the saved method in that flow.

The call flags and wallet presentment describe attempt and collection behavior. The preview registration request supplies no payment API version or wallet configuration.

payments-orchestration-wallet-payments.text: Enter your email to request access.
If the customer is present in your checkout flow, you can’t reuse a saved payment method.
Enable Apple Pay or Google Pay payment methods on your third-party processor.
You can use [Payment Links](https://docs.stripe.com/payment-links.md) to quickly test
Orchestration supports wallet payments including Apple Pay and Google Pay.
make sure to pass `off_session=true` during PaymentIntent confirmation

payments-orchestration-wallet-payments.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/orchestration/wallet-payments, November documents private-preview Orchestration routing for Apple Pay and Google Pay across eligible processors. Enable the applicable wallet on the third-party processor under its own requirements and configure Stripe using the relevant Apple Pay or Google Pay integration. Use Dashboard Payments > Orchestration > Rules for test routing and optionally Payment Links for a quick routing test (new raw lines 23-38). For an attempted charge on a saved mobile-wallet payment method, pass off_session=true when confirming the PaymentIntent. A customer present in checkout must be re-prompted through Apple Pay or Google Pay and cannot reuse the saved method. Those distinctions and steps are in old raw lines 6-21. The revised source-stripe-orchestration-wallet-payments.md retains routing, both checkout cases and Payment Links testing from baseline lines 13–19, with the processor and Stripe configuration, Dashboard test step and November preview request context added (new raw lines 7-21).
payments-orchestration-wallet-payments.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/orchestration/wallet-payments, November adds a private-preview notice and email request with the orchestration_preview registration example (new raw lines 7-21; old raw lines 4-21). The May overview already records private-preview status (raw/stripe-orchestration-2026.md lines 8–10). The anchor only navigates to the request, and the remaining diff changes spacing and list presentation. The revised source preserves the dated May setup, saved-wallet PaymentIntent confirmation and customer-present re-prompt guidance. It reconciles source-stripe-orchestration-wallet-payments.md, the concept and the feature matrix on general Apple Pay and Google Pay support across Adyen, Braintree and Worldpay WPG, with 3DS unsupported for either wallet’s DPAN and Google Pay FPAN unsupported on Adyen (November feature-support raw lines 35–53). off_session=true belongs to PaymentIntent confirmation of a saved-wallet charge attempt, while the on-session presentment belongs to the wallet integration. The preview example is an access request. It supplies no account entitlement, payment API version or wallet configuration. Sandbox rules and Payment Links testing supply no evidence of live rule activation (November Rules raw lines 63–75) or payment, capture or settlement outcomes.
